docs.title: m365-gdap-runner
docs.text:
Run a Python script across every customer tenant you reach through GDAP, from a single partner sign-in. The runner owns the loop: sign-in, tenant selection, consent checks, error isolation and parallelism. Authentication and the service clients come from azure-auth. A script contains neither; it holds the work for one tenant and its own reports.

  • Getting started: install the commands, set up, and run a first script.
  • Usage: writing scripts, choosing tenants, sign-ins, reports and settings.
  • Development: set up a development environment for the package itself.
  • Reference: the API, from the docstrings.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: Setting up a working copy, to change the package itself.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• uv. It fetches the Python version pinned in .python-version, 3.11, when the system has none.
  • git.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/DrollRobot/m365-gdap-runner.git
cd m365-gdap-runner
uv sync
uv run pre-commit install
uv run pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The working copy reads the same config file and tenants file as an installed copy. To keep others for development, point M365_GDAP_RUNNER_CONFIG_DIR at another directory, and run m365-gdap-runner-config init there:

export M365_GDAP_RUNNER_CONFIG_DIR=~/m365-gdap-runner-dev
uv run m365-gdap-runner-config init

docs.title: Running a script against the working copy
docs.text:
A script's header names a release of the runner, so uv run script.py runs that release. To run a script against the working copy instead, run it with the project's Python:

uv run python path/to/script.py --include pilot

Anything else the script's header names must then be in the project's environment too.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: See AGENTS.TESTING.md in the repository root.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
uv run mkdocs serve           # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
uv run mkdocs build --strict  # build, failing on any warning

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• uv. It fetches Python 3.11 or newer when the system has none.
  • A partner account with GDAP access to the customer tenants you want to run scripts against.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The package has two commands: m365-gdap-runner-config sets up the configuration, and m365-gdap-runner-customer-export creates the tenants file. Install them with:

uv tool install git+https://github.com/DrollRobot/m365-gdap-runner.git

Scripts do not need this install: each one names the library in its header, and uv run builds the script's own environment from that.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
m365-gdap-runner-config init

It asks for each setting in turn. Two are required: partner_tenant_id, the partner tenant's ID or domain name, and username, the partner account you sign in with. Press Enter at the others to keep their defaults; Settings lists them all.

docs.title: Create the tenants file
docs.text:
m365-gdap-runner-customer-export

It signs in as the partner account, in the browser, lists every tenant with a GDAP relationship, and writes them to tenants.csv in the config directory (m365-gdap-runner-config path shows where).

Open the file in a spreadsheet and add a group column: a header such as pilot, and TRUE in the rows of two or three tenants to try a first script on. A blank cell counts as FALSE.

docs.title: Write a script
docs.text:
Save this as users.py:

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "m365-gdap-runner @ git+https://github.com/DrollRobot/m365-gdap-runner.git@v0.2.0",
# ]
# ///
from m365_gdap_runner import TenantContext, TenantResult

CLIENTS = ["graph"]  # which of ctx.graph, ctx.exchange, ctx.ipps, ctx.arm you use
SCOPES = ["User.Read.All"]  # delegated Graph scopes; only when "graph" is in CLIENTS


def run(ctx: TenantContext) -> list[str]:
    users = ctx.graph.get_all("/users", params={"$select": "userPrincipalName"})
    return [u["userPrincipalName"] for u in users]


def report(results: list[TenantResult]) -> None:
    for result in results:
        print(result.tenant.display_name, result.status, len(result.result or []))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from m365_gdap_runner import main

    raise SystemExit(main(__name__))

run(ctx) does the work for one tenant. report(results) is optional; it gets every tenant's result once the last one is done.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
uv run users.py --include pilot

The runner signs in at the partner tenant, in the browser, checks each tenant in the pilot group through that sign-in, and calls run() for each one. Logs and a summary go to stderr; what report() prints goes to stdout.

--include also takes a single tenant, by display name or ID, or all for every GDAP tenant:

uv run users.py --include Contoso

uv run users.py -h lists every flag. Usage covers the rest.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
A script is a .py file that does the work for one tenant; the runner calls it once per selected tenant. It defines run(ctx), declares what it uses, and hands itself to the library from its __main__ block:

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "m365-gdap-runner @ git+https://github.com/DrollRobot/m365-gdap-runner.git@v0.2.0",
# ]
# ///
from m365_gdap_runner import TenantContext

CLIENTS = ["graph", "exchange"]
SCOPES = ["User.Read.All"]
CONTINUE_ON_ERROR = True


def run(ctx: TenantContext) -> dict[str, object]:
    users = ctx.graph.get_all("/users", params={"$select": "userPrincipalName"})
    (config,) = ctx.exchange.run("Get-OrganizationConfig")
    return {"users": len(users), "audit_disabled": config["AuditDisabled"]}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from m365_gdap_runner import main

    raise SystemExit(main(__name__))

The header at the top tells uv what the script needs: the runner, at a release, and anything else the script imports, such as a library for its reports. uv run script.py builds the script's own environment from it.

docs.title: What a script declares
docs.text:
• run(ctx): the work for one tenant. ctx is the tenant's context; what run() returns is kept, as it is, in the tenant's result.
  • CLIENTS: which of ctx.graph, ctx.exchange, ctx.ipps and ctx.arm the script uses. Default ["graph"].
  • SCOPES: the delegated Graph scopes the script needs in each tenant. Required when graph is in CLIENTS, not allowed otherwise. See Scopes.
  • report(results), optional: called once after the last tenant. See Reports.
  • CONTINUE_ON_ERROR, optional: keep going after an error in run(). See Errors in run().
  • GRANT_WHEN_POSSIBLE, optional: add missing scopes to the app's grant where it can. See Granting missing scopes.

The script is checked before any sign-in, so a mistake in it never costs a browser prompt.

docs.title: The tenant context
docs.text:
run(ctx) gets a TenantContext for the tenant:

  • ctx.tenant: the tenant, with its tenant_id, display_name and cloud.
  • ctx.graph: Microsoft Graph.
  • ctx.exchange: Exchange Online.
  • ctx.ipps: Security & Compliance PowerShell.
  • ctx.arm: Azure Resource Manager.
  • ctx.auth: the azure-auth context for the tenant. Hand it to any azure-auth client, or to an Azure SDK client as credential=, for resources the four clients do not cover.

The clients come from azure-auth, which documents what each one offers. Each client in CLIENTS is checked in the tenant before run() starts, so run() never opens a sign-in window. Asking for a client the script did not declare raises ClientNotDeclared.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
The check before run() asks for exactly the scopes in SCOPES, so a tenant that has not granted one of them fails before run(). SCOPES = [] asks for none in particular: Graph gets whatever the app holds in the tenant, and only a tenant where it holds nothing fails. That suits a script that reads what the app holds, with ctx.graph.granted_scopes(). .default is refused, since it would skip the check.

An entry may be a tuple of scopes, any one of which will do:

SCOPES = [("Application.Read.All", "Application.ReadWrite.All")]

The check reads what each tenant has granted and asks for the first scope in the tuple the tenant holds. A tenant that holds none is asked for the first scope in the tuple, so the consent screen, the consent error and a self-grant name that one. Put the least-privileged scope first. A tenant that signs in on its own is asked for the first scope in each tuple, since what it has granted cannot be read before the sign-in.

docs.title: Flags of your own
docs.text:
main(__name__) reads the library's flags only. A script with flags of its own builds the parser, adds the library's with add_arguments(), and passes what it parsed to main(); -h then lists both:

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    from m365_gdap_runner import add_arguments, main

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Users in each tenant.")
    parser.add_argument("--domain", help="Only users in this domain.")
    add_arguments(parser)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    DOMAIN = args.domain
    raise SystemExit(main(__name__, args))

run() reads DOMAIN like any other module-level value. The script's own flag names must not clash with the library's.

docs.title: Choosing tenants
docs.text:
A run has to say which tenants it is for; one that includes none is refused. Pick them with --include, and take some back out with --exclude. Both are repeatable, and each takes:

  • a tenant, by display name or ID: a GDAP customer or a row of the tenants file.
  • a group: the tenants marked TRUE in that column of the tenants file.
  • all, for --include only: every tenant with a GDAP relationship.

Everything included adds up, and an exclusion always wins: --include all --exclude pilot runs every GDAP tenant outside the pilot group. Case does not matter. A name that matches nothing is an error, and so is one that could mean two things: a tenant and a group column with the same name, or a tenant or column named all. Name the tenant by its ID, or rename the column. --include m365_gdap runs the tenants the partner sign-in reaches (see Tenants outside GDAP).

docs.title: The tenants file
docs.text:
The tenants file is a CSV you edit in a spreadsheet, one row per customer. This package owns seven columns, m365_tenant_id, m365_tenant_name, m365_domain, m365_cloud, m365_username, m365_gdap and m365_pw_url, and reads one more per group a run names: a column holding TRUE or FALSE, where a blank cell counts as FALSE and anything else is an error. Every other column is left alone, so the same file can carry what other tools know about the same customers on other platforms.

m365_tenant_id,m365_tenant_name,m365_domain,m365_cloud,m365_username,m365_gdap,m365_pw_url,pilot,patching,crm_id
aaaaaaaa-0000-0000-0000-00000000000a,Alpha,alpha.example,Commercial,,TRUE,,TRUE,FALSE,1001
bbbbbbbb-0000-0000-0000-00000000000b,beta corp,beta.example,USGov,admin@beta.us,,https://passwords.example/beta,TRUE,TRUE,1002
cccccccc-0000-0000-0000-00000000000c,Gamma,gamma.example,Commercial,admin@gamma.example,FALSE,,FALSE,TRUE,1003

Tenants are matched by ID; the name and domain columns are there for you. A row with no m365_tenant_id is a customer without an M365 tenant and is skipped. A tenant may have more than one row, as long as they agree in every m365_ column; case and surrounding spaces do not count, and other columns may differ. A run that selects a tenant whose rows disagree is refused, naming the rows.

m365_cloud is Commercial, USGov, USGovDoD or China. m365_username, m365_gdap and m365_pw_url are covered in Tenants outside GDAP.

The file is tenants.csv in the config directory (m365-gdap-runner-config path shows where), unless the tenants_file setting or --tenants-file points elsewhere.

docs.title: Excel workbooks
docs.text:
The file can also be an Excel workbook, named .xlsx, with the same columns in one table (Insert > Table). The table may sit on any sheet, at any spot; a workbook with no table, or more than one, is an error. TRUE and FALSE may be Excel's own or typed as text, a totals row is ignored, and a formula counts as the value Excel last calculated.

When m365-gdap-runner-customer-export adds to the table, new columns go to its right and new rows below it, and the table grows to hold them; every other cell is left as it was. Those cells must be empty, and the table must have no totals row. Saving the workbook drops any charts and images in it. A missing .xlsx file is created as a workbook with one table.

docs.title: Keeping it up to date
docs.text:
Only the m365-gdap-runner-customer-export command writes the file. It creates the file when there is none. Any of the seven m365_ columns the file lacks is added after the m365_ columns it has (or at the end when it has none), blank, except that m365_gdap is TRUE for every tenant GDAP lists. A GDAP tenant with no row is appended with its name, its cloud, TRUE in m365_gdap and every other column blank, and a warning names it. A blank m365_cloud cell is filled in by OpenID Connect discovery. The command lists the tenants and runs nothing, so run it once to create the file, then add group columns. Rows for tenants without a GDAP relationship are yours to add and keep.

A script run never writes the file. Where the file falls behind, the run warns, names m365-gdap-runner-customer-export as the fix, and goes on as if the command had run, for that run only. With no file at all, it can pick only GDAP tenants.

docs.title: The partner sign-in
docs.text:
The runner signs in at the partner tenant as username, once per client in CLIENTS, since each client uses a different Microsoft app; client_id names one app for all of them instead.

Every selected tenant in the partner's cloud is then checked silently through that sign-in, jobs at a time; every 30 seconds, a log line says how many are done and about how long the rest will take. Each tenant's run() starts as soon as its access is settled.

Every sign-in, the partner's and each tenant's own, asks Microsoft for a new token for each client rather than trusting one saved by an earlier run. A saved token says nothing about whether Microsoft will still issue one: a Conditional Access policy may have started refusing the sign-in since. So that failure happens in the check, where a window may open, instead of inside run(), where none may.

Renewing your partner sign-in keeps the time you first signed in, and did multi-factor authentication. A customer whose Conditional Access policy allows less time refuses it however often it is renewed (AADSTS70043, or AADSTS50078 for the multi-factor authentication). The first such customer in a run opens a new partner sign-in that asks for your password, and multi-factor authentication, again: one window per client in CLIENTS. That customer, and every later one refused for the same reason, is then checked through the partner sign-in again. Only a tenant still refused goes to its own sign-in. Ctrl+C during that window, then Enter, skips it, and those customers go to their own sign-in.

docs.title: Sign-in windows
docs.text:
Sign-ins open the system's default browser. The Windows sign-in window (the broker) is not offered: GDAP does not work through it. To use another browser, or another profile of it:

  • browser_path: the browser, as a full path (recommended) or a program on PATH.
  • browser_args: a list of arguments for it, such as ["--profile-directory=Profile 2"]. The sign-in address is added last. Needs browser_path.

A sign-in window waits browser_timeout seconds (default 120) to be completed. After that, the sign-in fails: the partner sign-in ends the run, and a tenant's own leaves that tenant auth_failed.

To give up on a tenant's own sign-in without waiting, press Ctrl+C, then Enter: that tenant is auth_failed and the run goes on. Ctrl+C twice stops the run.

docs.title: Tenants outside GDAP
docs.text:
A tenant the partner sign-in cannot reach still runs. That covers a row of the tenants file with no GDAP relationship, a tenant in another cloud (the partner sign-in reaches its own cloud only), and a GDAP tenant where consent is missing or a policy wants a fresh sign-in.

Each tenant that fails the partner check, and each tenant in another cloud, gets a sign-in of its own, in its own cloud, as the account in its m365_username cell: one sign-in per client in CLIENTS. Sign-in windows open one at a time, as soon as a tenant needs one, while the other checks go on. A tenant's run() never opens a sign-in window. With --cache disk, later runs are silent. A sign-in that fails, is cancelled, times out or is skipped with Ctrl+C then Enter leaves that tenant auth_failed; the rest run.

A tenant whose m365_username cell is blank gets no sign-in of its own: it is auth_failed, with the reason, and no sign-in window opens for it.

m365_pw_url is optional: the address of the web page that holds that account's password, such as its entry in a password manager. When the tenant's own sign-in opens a window, the page opens right before it, once per tenant. It does not open when the sign-in comes from the cache. It opens in the system's default browser, or in pw_browser_path, started with pw_browser_args, such as ["--profile-directory=Default"]; the address is added last. Only http and https addresses are accepted.

The m365_gdap column says which tenants the partner sign-in reaches. TRUE, which every appended row gets, tries the partner sign-in first. FALSE or blank never tries it: the tenant goes straight to a sign-in of its own. GDAP can list a customer whose tenant it gives you no access to; put FALSE in that row's cell. With m365_username blank as well, the tenant is left out of the run, with a warning, instead of failing: that marks a customer you cannot reach at all but cannot remove from Partner Center. Anything else in the cell is an error.

m365_gdap is a group like any other, so --include m365_gdap runs only the tenants marked TRUE. A tenant there whose partner sign-in fails still gets a sign-in of its own when its m365_username is filled in.

docs.title: Consent
docs.text: A GDAP tenant whose grant lacks some of the script's scopes, where the app cannot add them itself, goes to its own sign-in with Entra's consent screen, whatever the cache holds. Tick "Consent on behalf of your organization" there. An administrator who consents for themselves alone leaves the partner sign-in without the scopes, and Entra never shows the screen again by itself for consent that exists. Granted for the organization, the tenant passes the partner check on the next run.

docs.title: Granting missing scopes
docs.text: A tenant whose grant lacks some of the script's SCOPES fails the check before the run. A script that sets GRANT_WHEN_POSSIBLE = True has the check add them instead, where the app holds DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All in that tenant. They go into the app's tenant-wide grant, so every user of the app there gets them, each still limited by their own roles. azure-auth logs each grant, which shows with -vv and in the debug log. The check then waits for a token that carries the new scopes: about a minute, three at most. Where the app does not hold that permission, the tenant gets a sign-in of its own as before. --grant-when-possible and --no-grant-when-possible override the script.

docs.title: Keeping sign-ins between runs
docs.text:
Sign-ins are kept in memory and end with the run. To keep them, opt in to the disk cache: the cache setting, or --cache, set to disk keeps them in an encrypted file, and later runs skip the sign-in. That includes each tenant's own sign-in: a tenant the partner sign-in cannot reach uses its cached sign-in, and opens the browser only when there is none.

The file is written after each sign-in, after each tenant, and when the run ends, so a run that is killed keeps what was written before. A run that finds the file empty, which a run killed while writing it could once leave, says so and names the file: delete it and sign in again.

The file holds refresh tokens, which sign in without a password. Two settings help keep track of it:

  • cache_path: the file to keep it in. Empty uses azure-auth's file in the per-user cache directory.
  • cache_reminder_path: a folder in plain sight, such as the Desktop. Every run with the disk cache puts M365-GDAP-RUNNER_MSAL_CACHE_DELETEME there, a link to the folder that holds the cache: a .url shortcut on Windows, a symbolic link elsewhere. It holds only a path, so it is safe in a synced folder; the cache itself is not.

docs.title: Tenants at once
docs.text: A run works on one tenant at a time. The jobs setting changes that, and --jobs changes it for one run; the silent checks before each run() use the same number. 5-8 suits read-only reports; keep 1 for scripts that write unless they are idempotent.

docs.title: Errors in run()
docs.text:
An error raised in run() stops the run: that tenant is error, tenants already running finish, and the tenants not yet started are skipped. That keeps a script that changes things from repeating a broken change in every tenant. A script that only reads sets CONTINUE_ON_ERROR = True to keep going. --continue-on-error and --no-continue-on-error override the script.

A tenant that could not be reached is auth_failed and never stops the run.

docs.title: Stopping a run
docs.text: Ctrl+C stops the run. A tenant it interrupts is error; with jobs above 1, the tenants already running finish first. The tenants not yet started are skipped, and the summary is printed. During a tenant's own sign-in window, Ctrl+C asks first: Enter skips that tenant, and a second Ctrl+C stops the run.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
The library writes no output of its own; reports belong to the script, in whatever form it needs.

  • Per tenant: run(ctx) writes it, with ctx.tenant for the tenant's name and ID.
  • Per run: report(results), when the script has one, is called once after the last tenant. It gets one TenantResult per tenant in run order, failed ones included: tenant, status (ok, auth_failed, error or skipped), result (whatever run() returned, as it is) and error.

report() is not called after Ctrl+C, since a report of part of a run would look complete. If it raises, the error is logged and the run exits with code 2. Logs and the summary go to stderr, so stdout is the script's.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Each log line names the tenant it belongs to, or - outside one, so lines from tenants run at once can be told apart. A script logs with Python's logging like any other program, and its records go to the same place, named the same way. -v adds debug lines from the runner and the script; -vv adds those of the libraries underneath, such as azure-auth and MSAL.

After the summary line, every warning and error the run logged is printed again, so none is lost in a long run's output. That includes the script's own warnings, and each tenant that failed, which logs an error.

A tenant's error, in the log and in its TenantResult, is one short line. For a tenant that could not be reached, it names each sign-in tried: partner: <why>; direct: <why>, such as partner: missing 5 of 19 Graph scopes, self-grant failed; direct: no m365_username. Missing consent is counted, not listed. Microsoft's Trace ID, Correlation ID and Timestamp are left out, and a message over 300 characters is cut to its first sentence.

The debug_log_path setting appends every log record to a file, debug and library ones included, whatever -v says, and keeps every error in full. A folder there means m365_gdap_runner_debug.log in it. Past debug_log_max_mb megabytes (default 10; 0 for no limit), the file is compressed to <name>.1.gz and a new one started; the newest debug_log_keep compressed files (default 5) are kept, and older ones deleted.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0: every tenant was ok.
  • 1: at least one tenant was not.
  • 2: the run could not start, or report() failed: a usage, configuration, script, sign-in, tenant listing, tenants file or tenant selection error.
  • 130: the run was stopped with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Settings live in config.toml in the per-user config directory:

  • Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\m365_gdap_runner\config.toml
  • Linux: ~/.config/m365_gdap_runner/config.toml
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/m365_gdap_runner/config.toml

The M365_GDAP_RUNNER_CONFIG_DIR environment variable points at another directory instead. The tenants file lives in the same directory unless tenants_file says otherwise.

docs.title: The config command
docs.text:
m365-gdap-runner-config creates and edits the file; it never needs editing by hand.

Command What it does init Asks for each setting in turn and writes the file. --force starts over. show Shows every setting's value and where it came from. set KEY VALUE Sets one setting. A list takes commas between its items. unset KEY Removes a setting, so its default applies. path Prints the file's path. open Opens the file in the program the system has for it. list-profiles Lists the profiles, marking the default. use PROFILE Makes a profile the default.

docs.title: Every setting
docs.text: Setting Default What it is partner_tenant_id required The partner tenant's ID or verified domain name. username required The partner account that signs in. client_id empty One app to sign in with for every client; empty uses Microsoft's first-party apps. cloud empty The partner tenant's cloud: Commercial, USGov, USGovDoD or China; empty looks it up. tenants_file empty The tenants file; empty uses tenants.csv in the config directory. jobs 1 Tenants at once. cache memory memory, or disk to keep sign-ins between runs. cache_path empty The disk cache's file; empty uses azure-auth's. cache_reminder_path empty A folder for the cache's DELETEME link; empty puts none. browser_path empty The browser sign-in windows open in; empty uses the system default. browser_args empty Arguments for browser_path. browser_timeout 120 Seconds a sign-in window waits to be completed. pw_browser_path empty The browser a tenant's m365_pw_url opens in; empty uses the system default. pw_browser_args empty Arguments for pw_browser_path. debug_log_path empty The debug log file or folder; empty writes none. debug_log_max_mb 10 Megabytes the debug log grows to before it is compressed; 0 for no limit. debug_log_keep 5 Compressed debug logs kept besides the current one.

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text: A flag beats an environment variable, which beats config.toml, which beats the default. Every setting has an environment variable, its name upper-cased after M365_GDAP_RUNNER_: M365_GDAP_RUNNER_JOBS=5. A list takes commas there too. These settings also have a flag: --partner-tenant-id, --username, --client-id, --cloud, --tenants-file, --cache and --jobs.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text: A profile is a named set of settings in the same file, for more than one partner tenant or account. m365-gdap-runner-config init --profile NAME creates one, and --profile NAME on set, unset and show works on it. A run uses --profile, else the M365_GDAP_RUNNER_PROFILE environment variable, else the default profile that use sets.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Run a Python script across GDAP customer tenants from a single partner sign-in.

Authentication is azure-auth's job. This library signs in once per client the script uses, lists the customer tenants, and calls the script's run(ctx) for each one with error isolation and optional parallelism. After the last tenant, the script's report(results), when it has one, gets every tenant's result; the library writes no output of its own.

A script is a .py file with run(ctx), the Graph SCOPES it needs, and which CLIENTS it uses (graph by default; also exchange, ipps, arm). Its __main__ block hands it to :func:main::

from m365_gdap_runner import TenantContext, TenantResult

SCOPES = ["User.Read.All"]
CLIENTS = ["graph", "exchange"]

def run(ctx: TenantContext) -> dict[str, object]:
    users = ctx.graph.get_all("/users", params={"$select": "userPrincipalName"})
    (config,) = ctx.exchange.run("Get-OrganizationConfig")
    return {"users": len(users), "audit_disabled": config["AuditDisabled"]}

def report(results: list[TenantResult]) -> None:
    for result in results:
        print(result.tenant.display_name, result.status, result.result or result.error)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    from m365_gdap_runner import main

    raise SystemExit(main(__name__))

Run it with uv run my_script.py --include pilot, where pilot is a TRUE/FALSE column of the tenants file (see tenants.py); --include also takes a tenant, or all, and --exclude takes tenants and groups out. A script with flags of its own adds the library's to its parser with :func:add_arguments and passes the parsed result to :func:main.

docs.title: ClientNotDeclared
docs.text:
Bases: RuntimeError

Raised when a payload uses a client it did not list in CLIENTS.

Source code in src/m365_gdap_runner/context.py 
class ClientNotDeclared(RuntimeError):
    """Raised when a payload uses a client it did not list in ``CLIENTS``."""

    def __init__(self, kind: str) -> None:
        """Name the missing client.

        Args:
            kind: The client kind that was asked for.
        """

class PartnerSession:
    """One partner sign-in, and the customer tenants reachable from it.

    Attributes:
        auth: The home azure-auth context, for the partner tenant.
    """

    def __init__(
        self, settings: Settings, *, transport: httpx2.BaseTransport | None = None
    ) -> None:
        """Build the home context from settings. No sign-in happens yet.

        Args:
            settings: Resolved settings.
            transport: Optional httpx2 transport for every client this session builds (tests).

        Raises:
            ConfigError: If ``cache`` or ``cloud`` holds a value azure-auth does not know,
                ``browser_args`` is set without ``browser_path``, ``pw_browser_args`` without
                ``pw_browser_path``, or ``browser_timeout`` is not more than 0.
            azure_auth.AuthError: If the partner tenant cannot be looked up, or the disk
                cache cannot be encrypted on this platform.
            azure_auth.NetworkError: If the partner tenant's sign-in host cannot be reached.
        """
        if settings.cache not in CACHE_KINDS:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"cache must be one of {', '.join(CACHE_KINDS)}, not {settings.cache!r}."
            )
        if settings.browser_timeout <= 0:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"browser_timeout must be more than 0 seconds, not {settings.browser_timeout!r}."
            )
        tenant: str | azure_auth.Tenant = settings.partner_tenant_id
        if settings.cloud:
            try:
                cloud = get_cloud(settings.cloud)
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise ConfigError(str(exc)) from exc
            tenant = _partner_tenant(settings.partner_tenant_id, cloud)
        self._transport = transport
        self._settings = settings
        # None keeps the disk cache in azure-auth's default file.
        self._cache_path = Path(settings.cache_path).expanduser() if settings.cache_path else None
        self._browser = _browser(settings.browser_path, settings.browser_args)
        self._pw_browser = _browser(
            settings.pw_browser_path, settings.pw_browser_args, prefix="pw_"
        )
        # How check_access() found each tenant can be reached, by lower-cased tenant ID. It
        # writes and context_for() reads, on different threads, but never for the same tenant
        # at once: check_access() hands a tenant out only after writing its route.
        self._routes: dict[str, AuthContext | Exception] = {}
        # The Graph scopes each tenant is asked for, by lower-cased tenant ID: the script's,
        # with one scope chosen from each tuple (:func:`choose_scopes`). Written and read as
        # ``_routes`` is.
        self._scopes: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
        # Whether the partner tenant was signed in to again this run, for a customer that found
        # the sign-in too old: None until one does, then whether it worked.
        self._signed_in_again: bool | None = None
        self.auth = AuthContext(
            tenant,
            username=settings.username,
            client_id=settings.client_id or None,
            cache=cast(Literal["memory", "disk"], settings.cache),
            cache_path=self._cache_path,
            browser_timeout=settings.browser_timeout,
            browser=self._browser,
        )
        if settings.cache == "disk" and settings.cache_reminder_path:
            _place_cache_reminder(
                self._cache_path or default_cache_path(), settings.cache_reminder_path
            )

    @property
    def partner_tenant_id(self) -> str:
        """The partner tenant's GUID."""
        return self.auth.tenant.id

    @property
    def cloud_name(self) -> str:
        """Name of the cloud this session signs in to, as azure-auth spells it."""
        return self.auth.tenant.cloud.name

    def cloud_of(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
        """Find the cloud a tenant lives in, by OpenID Connect discovery.

        Discovery is unauthenticated and asks each public sign-in host once, so it costs
        three requests and works for any tenant. It fills the tenants file's ``m365_cloud``
        column.

        Args:
            tenant_id: The tenant's GUID.

        Returns:
            The cloud's name (``Commercial``, ``USGov``, ``USGovDoD`` or ``China``), or ``""``
            when no sign-in host knows the tenant or none can be reached.
        """
        try:
            return azure_auth.Tenant.lookup(tenant_id, transport=self._transport).cloud.name
        except (AuthError, NetworkError, ValueError) as exc:
            logger.debug("Could not look up the cloud of %s: %s", tenant_id, exc)
            return ""

    def login(self, clients: Iterable[str] = (), *, reauthenticate: bool = False) -> None:
        """Sign in at the partner tenant, once per client id the payload needs.

        Graph is always signed in, for listing customers. Each client asks Entra for a new
        token, so a sign-in window opens only for a client id with no usable cached sign-in,
        or one Entra will not renew. Each client's sign-in is written to the disk cache at
        once, so a run killed later keeps it.

        Args:
            clients: The payload's ``CLIENTS``.
            reauthenticate: Open a sign-in window for every client instead, and have Entra ask
                for the password again, and for multi-factor authentication where the partner
                tenant wants it, whatever the cache holds (azure-auth's ``login()`` option of
                that name).

        Raises:
            azure_auth.AuthError: If a sign-in fails or is cancelled.
            azure_auth.NetworkError: If Entra ID cannot be reached.
        """
        kinds = ["graph", *(kind for kind in clients if kind != "graph")]
        for kind in kinds:
            if kind not in CLIENT_KINDS:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown client kind {kind!r}.")
            logger.debug("Signing in to the partner tenant for %s", kind)
            scopes = PARTNER_SCOPES if kind == "graph" else ()
            with build_client(kind, self.auth, scopes=scopes, transport=self._transport) as client:
                # A sign-in that asked for the password got its token from Entra already.
                client.login(fresh=not reauthenticate, reauthenticate=reauthenticate)
            self.auth.flush_cache()

    def list_tenants(self) -> list[Tenant]:
        """List the customer tenants with a GDAP relationship to the partner.

        Returns:
            Tenants deduplicated by ID, sorted by display name. A customer without a display
            name is named by its ID.

        Raises:
            azure_auth.AuthError: If no partner token can be obtained.
            azure_auth.GraphError: If Graph rejects the request.
            azure_auth.NetworkError: If Entra ID or Graph cannot be reached.
        """
        with GraphClient(
            self.auth, scopes=list(PARTNER_SCOPES), transport=self._transport
        ) as graph:
            customers = graph.list_customers()
        tenants: dict[str, Tenant] = {}
        for customer in customers:
            tenant_id = str(customer["tenantId"])
            display_name = str(customer.get("displayName") or tenant_id)
            tenants.setdefault(tenant_id.lower(), Tenant(tenant_id, display_name))
        return sorted(
            tenants.values(), key=lambda t: (t.display_name.casefold(), t.tenant_id.lower())
        )

    def check_access(
        self,
        tenants: Sequence[Tenant],
        *,
        scopes: Sequence[Scope] = (),
        clients: Sequence[str] = ("graph",),
        jobs: int = 1,
        grant_when_possible: bool = False,
    ) -> Generator[Tenant, None, None]:
        """Find a way into each tenant, and hand it out as soon as one is found.

        A tenant in the partner's cloud is checked first through the partner sign-in, silently
        and the way the run will use it: every client the script uses must get a new token
        from Entra (:meth:`TenantContext.probe`). Where *scopes* has a tuple, the check reads
        what the tenant has granted first and asks for the first scope in the tuple it holds,
        or the first scope in the tuple where it holds none (:func:`choose_scopes`); a direct
        sign-in asks for the first scope in each tuple. With *grant_when_possible*, a tenant whose
        grant lacks some of *scopes* has them added to the app's grant there, when the app holds
        ``DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All``, and passes. A tenant whose policy finds the
        partner sign-in too old (AADSTS70043, AADSTS50078) has the partner tenant signed in to
        again, asking for the password, once a run (:meth:`_sign_in_again`), and is checked
        again. A tenant that fails that check, for whatever reason, a tenant in another cloud,
        and a tenant whose ``gdap`` is False, which is never checked, then get a direct
        sign-in: a context of their own, in their own cloud, as their ``username``, signed in
        once per client. One with no ``username`` gets none, and no prompt. A sign-in window
        opens only where no cached sign-in will do, except for a tenant whose check failed for
        missing consent: its Graph sign-in opens Entra's consent screen whatever the cache
        holds, for the tenant-wide grant (:meth:`_sign_in_directly`).

        The silent checks run in the background, *jobs* at a time. Direct sign-ins run on the
        thread that iterates, one at a time, as soon as a tenant needs one: the tenants never
        checked first, then each one whose check fails. Before each one, every tenant whose
        check has passed is handed out, so a sign-in window holds up no tenant that is ready.
        A log line every 30 seconds says how many checks are done and about how long the rest
        will take. Ctrl+C during a direct sign-in asks whether to skip that tenant, which
        leaves it unreachable, or stop the run, which raises KeyboardInterrupt from here.
        Stopping the iteration (``close()``) cancels the checks not yet started and opens no
        more sign-in windows.

        :meth:`context_for` then hands out what was found, and raises the reason for a tenant
        that could not be reached.

        Args:
            tenants: The selected tenants, with their cloud filled in.
            scopes: The script's Graph scopes.
            clients: The script's ``CLIENTS``.
            jobs: How many silent checks run at once.
            grant_when_possible: Add the scopes a tenant lacks to the app's grant where the
                app can, through the partner sign-in only (azure-auth's ``GraphClient`` option
                of that name). Each grant waits for a token that carries the new scopes,
                about a minute and three at most.

        Yields:
            Each tenant once, as soon as :meth:`context_for` can hand out its context or the
            reason it could not be reached.
        """
        partner_cloud = self.cloud_name.lower()
        nearby = [
            t for t in tenants if t.gdap and (t.cloud or self.cloud_name).lower() == partner_cloud
        ]
        checked_ids = {t.tenant_id.lower() for t in nearby}
        # Tenants waiting for a direct sign-in, each with why the partner sign-in failed, or
        # None when it was never tried.
        direct: deque[tuple[Tenant, Exception | None]] = deque(
            (t, None) for t in tenants if t.tenant_id.lower() not in checked_ids
        )
        logger.info("Checking access to %d tenant(s)", len(tenants))
        done = 0
        started = last = monotonic()
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(
            max_workers=max(1, min(jobs, len(nearby))), thread_name_prefix="check"
        ) as pool:
            checks = {
                pool.submit(self._through_partner, t, scopes, clients, grant_when_possible): t
                for t in nearby
            }
            position = {future: index for index, future in enumerate(checks)}
            waiting = set(checks)
            try:
                while waiting or direct:
                    # Wait for a check only when no sign-in is waiting to be done.
                    finished, waiting = wait(
                        waiting, timeout=0 if direct else None, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED
                    )
                    for future in sorted(finished, key=position.__getitem__):
                        tenant, route = checks[future], future.result()
                        done += 1
                        now = monotonic()
                        if done < len(nearby) and now - last >= _PROGRESS_EVERY:
                            last = now
                            left = (now - started) / done * (len(nearby) - done)
                            logger.info(
                                "Checked %d of %d tenant(s), %s",
                                done,
                                len(nearby),
                                _time_left(left),
                            )
                        if not isinstance(route, AuthContext) and self._sign_in_again(
                            tenant, route, clients, grant_when_possible
                        ):
                            route = self._through_partner(
                                tenant, scopes, clients, grant_when_possible
                            )
                        if isinstance(route, AuthContext):
                            self._routes[tenant.tenant_id.lower()] = route
                            yield tenant
                        else:
                            direct.append((tenant, route))
                    if direct:
                        tenant, failure = direct.popleft()
                        self._routes[tenant.tenant_id.lower()] = self._reach_directly(
                            tenant, failure, scopes, clients, grant_when_possible
                        )
                        yield tenant
            finally:
                # On Ctrl+C, or when the run stops early, the checks not yet started never start.
                for future in checks:
                    future.cancel()

    def _sign_in_again(
        self,
        tenant: Tenant,
        failure: Exception,
        clients: Sequence[str],
        grant_when_possible: bool,
    ) -> bool:
        """Sign in at the partner tenant again, for a tenant that finds the sign-in too old.

        Renewing the partner sign-in keeps the time of the first one, and of its multi-factor
        authentication, so a customer whose policy allows less time refuses it however often
        it is renewed. A new sign-in that asks for the password again resets both. It opens
        one window per client, once a run, for the first tenant that needs it; a tenant that
        needs it after that is checked again without one. Ctrl+C during it asks whether to
        skip it, which sends the tenants that needed it to their own sign-in, or stop the run.

        Args:
            tenant: The tenant whose check through the partner sign-in failed.
            failure: Why it failed.
            clients: The script's ``CLIENTS``.
            grant_when_possible: As for :meth:`check_access`, for the reason logged.

        Returns:
            Whether to check the tenant through the partner sign-in again: the failure is one a
            new sign-in answers, and the partner tenant has been signed in to again.

        Raises:
            KeyboardInterrupt: When the person chooses to stop the run.
        """
        if not (isinstance(failure, AuthError) and failure.error_codes & _STALE_SIGN_IN_CODES):
            return False
        if self._signed_in_again is None:
            with tag_logs(tenant):
                logger.info(
                    "partner: %s; signing in to the partner tenant again",
                    brief(failure, grant_when_possible=grant_when_possible),
                )
            try:
                self.login(clients, reauthenticate=True)
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                _ask_to_skip("the partner tenant")
                self._signed_in_again = False
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.debug("Signing in to the partner tenant again failed", exc_info=True)
                logger.warning("Could not sign in to the partner tenant again: %s", brief(exc))
                self._signed_in_again = False
            else:
                self._signed_in_again = True
        return self._signed_in_again

    def _reach_directly(
        self,
        tenant: Tenant,
        failure: Exception | None,
        scopes: Sequence[Scope],
        clients: Sequence[str],
        grant_when_possible: bool,
    ) -> AuthContext | Exception:
        """Give a tenant the partner sign-in does not reach a sign-in of its own, if it can.

        The sign-in asks for the first scope in each tuple in *scopes*: what the tenant has
        granted cannot be read before it.

        Args:
            tenant: The tenant.
            failure: Why its check through the partner sign-in failed, or None when it had none:
                its ``gdap`` is False, or it is in another cloud.
            scopes: The script's Graph scopes.
            clients: The script's ``CLIENTS``.
            grant_when_possible: Whether that check could add missing scopes to the app's
                grant, for what the failure says of it.

        Returns:
            The tenant's own context, else why it cannot be reached, in short
            (:func:`~m365_gdap_runner.error_text.brief`): ``partner: <why>; direct: <why>``. A
            tenant with no ``username`` gets no sign-in, and no prompt.
        """
        if failure is not None:
            partner = brief(failure, grant_when_possible=grant_when_possible)
        elif not tenant.gdap:
            partner = "m365_gdap is FALSE"
        else:
            partner = f"tenant is in the {tenant.cloud} cloud"
        if not tenant.username:
            return AuthError(f"partner: {partner}; direct: no m365_username")
        chosen = choose_scopes(scopes, None)
        self._scopes[tenant.tenant_id.lower()] = chosen
        consent = isinstance(failure, ConsentRequired)
        with tag_logs(tenant):
            if consent:
                logger.info(
                    'partner: %s; direct: signing in as %s; tick "Consent on behalf of your '
                    'organization" in the consent screen',
                    partner,
                    tenant.username,
                )
            else:
                logger.info("partner: %s; direct: signing in as %s", partner, tenant.username)
            route = self._sign_in_directly(tenant, chosen, clients, consent=consent)
        if isinstance(route, AuthContext):
            return route
        return AuthError(f"partner: {partner}; direct: {route}")

    def _through_partner(
        self,
        tenant: Tenant,
        scopes: Sequence[Scope],
        clients: Sequence[str],
        grant_when_possible: bool,
    ) -> AuthContext | Exception:
        """Check a tenant through the partner sign-in, silently.

        Args:
            tenant: The tenant, in the partner's cloud.
            scopes: The script's Graph scopes.
            clients: The script's ``CLIENTS``.
            grant_when_possible: Add missing scopes to the app's grant where it can.

        Returns:
            The customer tenant's context when every client got a token, else what went wrong.
        """
        with tag_logs(tenant):
            try:
                auth = self.auth.get_tenant_context(tenant.tenant_id)
                chosen = self._choose_scopes(auth, scopes, clients)
                self._scopes[tenant.tenant_id.lower()] = chosen
                with TenantContext(
                    tenant,
                    auth,
                    scopes=chosen,
                    clients=clients,
                    grant_when_possible=grant_when_possible,
                    transport=self._transport,
                ) as context:
                    context.probe()
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.debug("The partner sign-in cannot reach the tenant", exc_info=True)
                return exc
            return auth

    def _choose_scopes(
        self, auth: AuthContext, scopes: Sequence[Scope], clients: Sequence[str]
    ) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Pick the scope to ask a tenant for from each tuple in the script's scopes.

        Where *scopes* has a tuple and the script uses Graph, the tenant's grant is read
        through *auth* (azure-auth's ``granted_scopes()``: one silent request to Entra, no
        prompt). A grant that cannot be read leaves each tuple its first scope, and the check
        that follows raises the reason, if it is one.

        Args:
            auth: The tenant's context, through the partner sign-in.
            scopes: The script's Graph scopes.
            clients: The script's ``CLIENTS``.

        Returns:
            One scope per entry (:func:`choose_scopes`).
        """
        if "graph" not in clients or all(isinstance(entry, str) for entry in scopes):
            return choose_scopes(scopes, None)
        granted: frozenset[str] | None = None
        try:
            with build_client("graph", auth, transport=self._transport) as client:
                assert isinstance(client, GraphClient)  # noqa: S101
                granted = client.granted_scopes()
        except AuthError:
            logger.debug("The tenant's grant cannot be read", exc_info=True)
        chosen = choose_scopes(scopes, granted)
        logger.debug("Asking for Graph scopes %s", ", ".join(chosen))
        return chosen

    def _sign_in_directly(
        self,
        tenant: Tenant,
        scopes: Sequence[str],
        clients: Sequence[str],
        *,
        consent: bool = False,
    ) -> AuthContext | str:
        """Sign in to a tenant on its own, as its own account, once per client the script uses.

        Each client asks Entra for a new token, as :meth:`TenantContext.probe` does, so a
        cached sign-in that Entra has stopped renewing opens the window here, where it may.
        With *consent*, the Graph sign-in opens the window whatever the cache holds and has
        Entra show its consent screen for the script's scopes (azure-auth's ``login()`` option
        of that name): a tenant whose consent is one user's own never shows it again by
        itself, and an administrator can tick "Consent on behalf of your organization" there.
        Ctrl+C while it waits asks whether to skip the tenant or stop the run
        (:func:`_ask_to_skip`).

        Args:
            tenant: The tenant, with its cloud and username filled in.
            scopes: The script's Graph scopes.
            clients: The script's ``CLIENTS``.
            consent: Whether the partner sign-in failed for missing consent, so the Graph
                sign-in should show the consent screen.

        Returns:
            The tenant's own context, signed in to every client, else what went wrong, in
            short.

        Raises:
            KeyboardInterrupt: When the person chooses to stop the run.
        """
        try:
            cloud = get_cloud(tenant.cloud or self.cloud_name)
            auth = AuthContext(
                azure_auth.Tenant(tenant.tenant_id, cloud),
                username=tenant.username,
                client_id=self._settings.client_id or None,
                cache=cast(Literal["memory", "disk"], self._settings.cache),
                cache_path=self._cache_path,
                browser_timeout=self._settings.browser_timeout,
                browser=self._browser,
                before_browser_opens=self._pw_page_opener(tenant),
            )
            for kind in clients:
                with build_client(kind, auth, scopes=scopes, transport=self._transport) as client:
                    # The consent screen is Graph's; a sign-in that showed it got its token
                    # from Entra already.
                    wants_consent = consent and kind == "graph"
                    client.login(consent=wants_consent, fresh=not wants_consent)
            # Written now, so a run killed later keeps the sign-in it may have asked for.
            auth.flush_cache()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            _ask_to_skip(tenant.display_name)
            return "skipped with Ctrl+C"
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.debug("The direct sign-in failed", exc_info=True)
            why = brief(exc)
            logger.warning("Could not sign in as %s: %s", tenant.username, why)
            return why
        return auth

    def _pw_page_opener(self, tenant: Tenant) -> Callable[[], None] | None:
        """Build what opens a tenant's password page with its first sign-in window.

        Args:
            tenant: The tenant, about to sign in directly.

        Returns:
            A function for azure-auth's ``before_browser_opens``, which opens the page the
            first time a window opens and does nothing after, so a script with several clients
            opens it once; or None when the tenant has no ``pw_url``.
        """
        if not tenant.pw_url:
            return None
        opened = False

        def open_once() -> None:
            nonlocal opened
            if not opened:
                opened = True
                _open_pw_page(tenant, self._pw_browser)

        return open_once

    def context_for(
        self, tenant: Tenant, *, scopes: Sequence[Scope] = (), clients: Sequence[str] = ("graph",)
    ) -> TenantContext:
        """Build the context a script receives for one customer tenant.

        Args:
            tenant: The customer tenant.
            scopes: The script's Graph scopes.
            clients: The script's ``CLIENTS``.

        Returns:
            The context, with one client per declared kind: on the route
            :meth:`check_access` found, asking for the scopes it chose there, or through the
            partner sign-in for a tenant it did not check, asking for the first scope in each
            tuple. No network call is made.

        Raises:
            Exception: Why :meth:`check_access` could not reach the tenant.
        """
        route = self._routes.get(tenant.tenant_id.lower())
        if isinstance(route, Exception):
            raise route
        chosen = self._scopes.get(tenant.tenant_id.lower()) or choose_scopes(scopes, None)
        return TenantContext(
            tenant,
            route or self.auth.get_tenant_context(tenant.tenant_id),
            scopes=chosen,
            clients=clients,
            transport=self._transport,
        )

def __init__(
    self, settings: Settings, *, transport: httpx2.BaseTransport | None = None
) -> None:
    """Build the home context from settings. No sign-in happens yet.

    Args:
        settings: Resolved settings.
        transport: Optional httpx2 transport for every client this session builds (tests).

    Raises:
        ConfigError: If ``cache`` or ``cloud`` holds a value azure-auth does not know,
            ``browser_args`` is set without ``browser_path``, ``pw_browser_args`` without
            ``pw_browser_path``, or ``browser_timeout`` is not more than 0.
        azure_auth.AuthError: If the partner tenant cannot be looked up, or the disk
            cache cannot be encrypted on this platform.
        azure_auth.NetworkError: If the partner tenant's sign-in host cannot be reached.
    """
    if settings.cache not in CACHE_KINDS:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"cache must be one of {', '.join(CACHE_KINDS)}, not {settings.cache!r}."
        )
    if settings.browser_timeout <= 0:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"browser_timeout must be more than 0 seconds, not {settings.browser_timeout!r}."
        )
    tenant: str | azure_auth.Tenant = settings.partner_tenant_id
    if settings.cloud:
        try:
            cloud = get_cloud(settings.cloud)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ConfigError(str(exc)) from exc
        tenant = _partner_tenant(settings.partner_tenant_id, cloud)
    self._transport = transport
    self._settings = settings
    # None keeps the disk cache in azure-auth's default file.
    self._cache_path = Path(settings.cache_path).expanduser() if settings.cache_path else None
    self._browser = _browser(settings.browser_path, settings.browser_args)
    self._pw_browser = _browser(
        settings.pw_browser_path, settings.pw_browser_args, prefix="pw_"
    )
    # How check_access() found each tenant can be reached, by lower-cased tenant ID. It
    # writes and context_for() reads, on different threads, but never for the same tenant
    # at once: check_access() hands a tenant out only after writing its route.
    self._routes: dict[str, AuthContext | Exception] = {}
    # The Graph scopes each tenant is asked for, by lower-cased tenant ID: the script's,
    # with one scope chosen from each tuple (:func:`choose_scopes`). Written and read as
    # ``_routes`` is.
    self._scopes: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    # Whether the partner tenant was signed in to again this run, for a customer that found
    # the sign-in too old: None until one does, then whether it worked.
    self._signed_in_again: bool | None = None
    self.auth = AuthContext(
        tenant,
        username=settings.username,
        client_id=settings.client_id or None,
        cache=cast(Literal["memory", "disk"], settings.cache),
        cache_path=self._cache_path,
        browser_timeout=settings.browser_timeout,
        browser=self._browser,
    )
    if settings.cache == "disk" and settings.cache_reminder_path:
        _place_cache_reminder(
            self._cache_path or default_cache_path(), settings.cache_reminder_path
        )

Find a way into each tenant, and hand it out as soon as one is found.

A tenant in the partner's cloud is checked first through the partner sign-in, silently and the way the run will use it: every client the script uses must get a new token from Entra (:meth:TenantContext.probe). Where scopes has a tuple, the check reads what the tenant has granted first and asks for the first scope in the tuple it holds, or the first scope in the tuple where it holds none (:func:choose_scopes); a direct sign-in asks for the first scope in each tuple. With grant_when_possible, a tenant whose grant lacks some of scopes has them added to the app's grant there, when the app holds DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All, and passes. A tenant whose policy finds the partner sign-in too old (AADSTS70043, AADSTS50078) has the partner tenant signed in to again, asking for the password, once a run (:meth:_sign_in_again), and is checked again. A tenant that fails that check, for whatever reason, a tenant in another cloud, and a tenant whose gdap is False, which is never checked, then get a direct sign-in: a context of their own, in their own cloud, as their username, signed in once per client. One with no username gets none, and no prompt. A sign-in window opens only where no cached sign-in will do, except for a tenant whose check failed for missing consent: its Graph sign-in opens Entra's consent screen whatever the cache holds, for the tenant-wide grant (:meth:_sign_in_directly).

The silent checks run in the background, jobs at a time. Direct sign-ins run on the thread that iterates, one at a time, as soon as a tenant needs one: the tenants never checked first, then each one whose check fails. Before each one, every tenant whose check has passed is handed out, so a sign-in window holds up no tenant that is ready. A log line every 30 seconds says how many checks are done and about how long the rest will take. Ctrl+C during a direct sign-in asks whether to skip that tenant, which leaves it unreachable, or stop the run, which raises KeyboardInterrupt from here. Stopping the iteration (close()) cancels the checks not yet started and opens no more sign-in windows.

:meth:context_for then hands out what was found, and raises the reason for a tenant that could not be reached.

def check_access(
    self,
    tenants: Sequence[Tenant],
    *,
    scopes: Sequence[Scope] = (),
    clients: Sequence[str] = ("graph",),
    jobs: int = 1,
    grant_when_possible: bool = False,
) -> Generator[Tenant, None, None]:
    """Find a way into each tenant, and hand it out as soon as one is found.

    A tenant in the partner's cloud is checked first through the partner sign-in, silently
    and the way the run will use it: every client the script uses must get a new token
    from Entra (:meth:`TenantContext.probe`). Where *scopes* has a tuple, the check reads
    what the tenant has granted first and asks for the first scope in the tuple it holds,
    or the first scope in the tuple where it holds none (:func:`choose_scopes`); a direct
    sign-in asks for the first scope in each tuple. With *grant_when_possible*, a tenant whose
    grant lacks some of *scopes* has them added to the app's grant there, when the app holds
    ``DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All``, and passes. A tenant whose policy finds the
    partner sign-in too old (AADSTS70043, AADSTS50078) has the partner tenant signed in to
    again, asking for the password, once a run (:meth:`_sign_in_again`), and is checked
    again. A tenant that fails that check, for whatever reason, a tenant in another cloud,
    and a tenant whose ``gdap`` is False, which is never checked, then get a direct
    sign-in: a context of their own, in their own cloud, as their ``username``, signed in
    once per client. One with no ``username`` gets none, and no prompt. A sign-in window
    opens only where no cached sign-in will do, except for a tenant whose check failed for
    missing consent: its Graph sign-in opens Entra's consent screen whatever the cache
    holds, for the tenant-wide grant (:meth:`_sign_in_directly`).

    The silent checks run in the background, *jobs* at a time. Direct sign-ins run on the
    thread that iterates, one at a time, as soon as a tenant needs one: the tenants never
    checked first, then each one whose check fails. Before each one, every tenant whose
    check has passed is handed out, so a sign-in window holds up no tenant that is ready.
    A log line every 30 seconds says how many checks are done and about how long the rest
    will take. Ctrl+C during a direct sign-in asks whether to skip that tenant, which
    leaves it unreachable, or stop the run, which raises KeyboardInterrupt from here.
    Stopping the iteration (``close()``) cancels the checks not yet started and opens no
    more sign-in windows.

    :meth:`context_for` then hands out what was found, and raises the reason for a tenant
    that could not be reached.

    Args:
        tenants: The selected tenants, with their cloud filled in.
        scopes: The script's Graph scopes.
        clients: The script's ``CLIENTS``.
        jobs: How many silent checks run at once.
        grant_when_possible: Add the scopes a tenant lacks to the app's grant where the
            app can, through the partner sign-in only (azure-auth's ``GraphClient`` option
            of that name). Each grant waits for a token that carries the new scopes,
            about a minute and three at most.

    Yields:
        Each tenant once, as soon as :meth:`context_for` can hand out its context or the
        reason it could not be reached.
    """
    partner_cloud = self.cloud_name.lower()
    nearby = [
        t for t in tenants if t.gdap and (t.cloud or self.cloud_name).lower() == partner_cloud
    ]
    checked_ids = {t.tenant_id.lower() for t in nearby}
    # Tenants waiting for a direct sign-in, each with why the partner sign-in failed, or
    # None when it was never tried.
    direct: deque[tuple[Tenant, Exception | None]] = deque(
        (t, None) for t in tenants if t.tenant_id.lower() not in checked_ids
    )
    logger.info("Checking access to %d tenant(s)", len(tenants))
    done = 0
    started = last = monotonic()
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(
        max_workers=max(1, min(jobs, len(nearby))), thread_name_prefix="check"
    ) as pool:
        checks = {
            pool.submit(self._through_partner, t, scopes, clients, grant_when_possible): t
            for t in nearby
        }
        position = {future: index for index, future in enumerate(checks)}
        waiting = set(checks)
        try:
            while waiting or direct:
                # Wait for a check only when no sign-in is waiting to be done.
                finished, waiting = wait(
                    waiting, timeout=0 if direct else None, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED
                )
                for future in sorted(finished, key=position.__getitem__):
                    tenant, route = checks[future], future.result()
                    done += 1
                    now = monotonic()
                    if done < len(nearby) and now - last >= _PROGRESS_EVERY:
                        last = now
                        left = (now - started) / done * (len(nearby) - done)
                        logger.info(
                            "Checked %d of %d tenant(s), %s",
                            done,
                            len(nearby),
                            _time_left(left),
                        )
                    if not isinstance(route, AuthContext) and self._sign_in_again(
                        tenant, route, clients, grant_when_possible
                    ):
                        route = self._through_partner(
                            tenant, scopes, clients, grant_when_possible
                        )
                    if isinstance(route, AuthContext):
                        self._routes[tenant.tenant_id.lower()] = route
                        yield tenant
                    else:
                        direct.append((tenant, route))
                if direct:
                    tenant, failure = direct.popleft()
                    self._routes[tenant.tenant_id.lower()] = self._reach_directly(
                        tenant, failure, scopes, clients, grant_when_possible
                    )
                    yield tenant
        finally:
            # On Ctrl+C, or when the run stops early, the checks not yet started never start.
            for future in checks:
                future.cancel()

def cloud_of(self, tenant_id: str) -> str:
    """Find the cloud a tenant lives in, by OpenID Connect discovery.

    Discovery is unauthenticated and asks each public sign-in host once, so it costs
    three requests and works for any tenant. It fills the tenants file's ``m365_cloud``
    column.

    Args:
        tenant_id: The tenant's GUID.

    Returns:
        The cloud's name (``Commercial``, ``USGov``, ``USGovDoD`` or ``China``), or ``""``
        when no sign-in host knows the tenant or none can be reached.
    """
    try:
        return azure_auth.Tenant.lookup(tenant_id, transport=self._transport).cloud.name
    except (AuthError, NetworkError, ValueError) as exc:
        logger.debug("Could not look up the cloud of %s: %s", tenant_id, exc)
        return ""

def context_for(
    self, tenant: Tenant, *, scopes: Sequence[Scope] = (), clients: Sequence[str] = ("graph",)
) -> TenantContext:
    """Build the context a script receives for one customer tenant.

    Args:
        tenant: The customer tenant.
        scopes: The script's Graph scopes.
        clients: The script's ``CLIENTS``.

    Returns:
        The context, with one client per declared kind: on the route
        :meth:`check_access` found, asking for the scopes it chose there, or through the
        partner sign-in for a tenant it did not check, asking for the first scope in each
        tuple. No network call is made.

    Raises:
        Exception: Why :meth:`check_access` could not reach the tenant.
    """
    route = self._routes.get(tenant.tenant_id.lower())
    if isinstance(route, Exception):
        raise route
    chosen = self._scopes.get(tenant.tenant_id.lower()) or choose_scopes(scopes, None)
    return TenantContext(
        tenant,
        route or self.auth.get_tenant_context(tenant.tenant_id),
        scopes=chosen,
        clients=clients,
        transport=self._transport,
    )

def list_tenants(self) -> list[Tenant]:
    """List the customer tenants with a GDAP relationship to the partner.

    Returns:
        Tenants deduplicated by ID, sorted by display name. A customer without a display
        name is named by its ID.

    Raises:
        azure_auth.AuthError: If no partner token can be obtained.
        azure_auth.GraphError: If Graph rejects the request.
        azure_auth.NetworkError: If Entra ID or Graph cannot be reached.
    """
    with GraphClient(
        self.auth, scopes=list(PARTNER_SCOPES), transport=self._transport
    ) as graph:
        customers = graph.list_customers()
    tenants: dict[str, Tenant] = {}
    for customer in customers:
        tenant_id = str(customer["tenantId"])
        display_name = str(customer.get("displayName") or tenant_id)
        tenants.setdefault(tenant_id.lower(), Tenant(tenant_id, display_name))
    return sorted(
        tenants.values(), key=lambda t: (t.display_name.casefold(), t.tenant_id.lower())
    )

def login(self, clients: Iterable[str] = (), *, reauthenticate: bool = False) -> None:
    """Sign in at the partner tenant, once per client id the payload needs.

    Graph is always signed in, for listing customers. Each client asks Entra for a new
    token, so a sign-in window opens only for a client id with no usable cached sign-in,
    or one Entra will not renew. Each client's sign-in is written to the disk cache at
    once, so a run killed later keeps it.

    Args:
        clients: The payload's ``CLIENTS``.
        reauthenticate: Open a sign-in window for every client instead, and have Entra ask
            for the password again, and for multi-factor authentication where the partner
            tenant wants it, whatever the cache holds (azure-auth's ``login()`` option of
            that name).

    Raises:
        azure_auth.AuthError: If a sign-in fails or is cancelled.
        azure_auth.NetworkError: If Entra ID cannot be reached.
    """
    kinds = ["graph", *(kind for kind in clients if kind != "graph")]
    for kind in kinds:
        if kind not in CLIENT_KINDS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown client kind {kind!r}.")
        logger.debug("Signing in to the partner tenant for %s", kind)
        scopes = PARTNER_SCOPES if kind == "graph" else ()
        with build_client(kind, self.auth, scopes=scopes, transport=self._transport) as client:
            # A sign-in that asked for the password got its token from Entra already.
            client.login(fresh=not reauthenticate, reauthenticate=reauthenticate)
        self.auth.flush_cache()

class TenantContext:
    """Everything a payload's ``run()`` receives for one tenant.

    Attributes:
        tenant: The tenant being processed.
        auth: The azure-auth context for this tenant. Pass it to any azure-auth client, or
            to an Azure SDK client as ``credential=``, for resources not covered below.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        tenant: Tenant,
        auth: AuthContext,
        *,
        scopes: Sequence[str] = (),
        clients: Sequence[str] = ("graph",),
        grant_when_possible: bool = False,
        transport: httpx2.BaseTransport | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Build one client per declared kind. No network call is made.

        Args:
            tenant: The tenant being processed.
            auth: The azure-auth context for this tenant.
            scopes: The payload's Graph scopes.
            clients: The payload's ``CLIENTS``.
            grant_when_possible: Whether the Graph client adds missing scopes to the app's
                grant where it can.
            transport: Optional httpx2 transport for every client (tests).
        """
        self.tenant = tenant
        self.auth = auth
        self._clients: dict[str, ResourceClient] = {
            kind: build_client(
                kind,
                auth,
                scopes=scopes,
                grant_when_possible=grant_when_possible,
                transport=transport,
            )
            for kind in clients
        }

    @property
    def clients(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """The client kinds this context holds, as declared by the payload."""
        return tuple(self._clients)

    def _client(self, kind: str) -> ResourceClient:
        """Return a declared client.

        Args:
            kind: The client kind.

        Returns:
            The client.

        Raises:
            ClientNotDeclared: If the payload did not declare *kind*.
        """
        try:
            return self._clients[kind]
        except KeyError:
            raise ClientNotDeclared(kind) from None

    @property
    def graph(self) -> GraphClient:
        """Microsoft Graph client bound to this tenant and the payload's Graph scopes."""
        client = self._client("graph")
        assert isinstance(client, GraphClient)  # noqa: S101 (narrowing; build_client guarantees it)
        return client

    @property
    def exchange(self) -> ExchangeClient:
        """Exchange Online cmdlet client bound to this tenant."""
        client = self._client("exchange")
        assert isinstance(client, ExchangeClient)  # noqa: S101
        return client

    @property
    def ipps(self) -> IppsClient:
        """Security & Compliance cmdlet client bound to this tenant."""
        client = self._client("ipps")
        assert isinstance(client, IppsClient)  # noqa: S101
        return client

    @property
    def arm(self) -> ArmClient:
        """Azure Resource Manager client bound to this tenant."""
        client = self._client("arm")
        assert isinstance(client, ArmClient)  # noqa: S101
        return client

    def probe(self) -> None:
        """Get a new token from Entra for every declared client, without prompting.

        This is the check :meth:`~m365_gdap_runner.session.PartnerSession.check_access` makes
        before the run. Each client asks Entra for a new token even when the cache holds a
        usable one: a cached token says nothing about whether Entra still issues them, and the
        run trusts this check for up to an hour. A context from azure-auth's
        ``get_tenant_context()`` never opens a browser, so a scope that is not consented in this
        tenant, or a Conditional Access policy that has started refusing the sign-in, fails here
        instead of inside the script.

        Raises:
            azure_auth.ConsentRequired: If consent is missing in this tenant.
            azure_auth.InteractionRequired: If the tenant wants a sign-in.
            azure_auth.AuthError: For any other token failure.
            azure_auth.NetworkError: If Entra ID cannot be reached.
        """
        for client in self._clients.values():
            client.login(fresh=True)

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close every client's HTTP connections, and write the tenant's tokens to the disk cache.

        The disk cache is written once here for every token the tenant got, rather than once
        per token (azure-auth's ``flush_cache()``). With the memory cache there is nothing to
        write.
        """
        for client in self._clients.values():
            client.close()
        self.auth.flush_cache()

    def __enter__(self) -> Self:
        """Enter the context manager.

        Returns:
            This context.
        """
        return self

    def __exit__(
        self,
        _exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
        _exc_value: BaseException | None,
        _traceback: TracebackType | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Close the clients when leaving the context manager."""
        self.close()

def close(self) -> None:
    """Close every client's HTTP connections, and write the tenant's tokens to the disk cache.

    The disk cache is written once here for every token the tenant got, rather than once
    per token (azure-auth's ``flush_cache()``). With the memory cache there is nothing to
    write.

    for client in self._clients.values():

def probe(self) -> None:
    """Get a new token from Entra for every declared client, without prompting.

    This is the check :meth:`~m365_gdap_runner.session.PartnerSession.check_access` makes
    before the run. Each client asks Entra for a new token even when the cache holds a
    usable one: a cached token says nothing about whether Entra still issues them, and the
    run trusts this check for up to an hour. A context from azure-auth's
    ``get_tenant_context()`` never opens a browser, so a scope that is not consented in this
    tenant, or a Conditional Access policy that has started refusing the sign-in, fails here
    instead of inside the script.

    Raises:
        azure_auth.ConsentRequired: If consent is missing in this tenant.
        azure_auth.InteractionRequired: If the tenant wants a sign-in.
        azure_auth.AuthError: For any other token failure.
        azure_auth.NetworkError: If Entra ID cannot be reached.
    """
    for client in self._clients.values():
        client.login(fresh=True)
